title: images.dat
description:
images.dat holds the data of every image: one GRP graphic with its animation script, drawn as part of a sprite. A unit is usually several images: its body, its shadow, and overlays such as engine glows and turrets (see Appendix: Images list). Each entry gives the GRP file, how it turns and is clicked, whether it plays its full animation script, how it is drawn, its animation script, and six lists of points (overlay files) where other graphics attach. It is the file arr\images.dat in the game's MPQ archives and is 37962 bytes long. Each field below is a list with one entry for each of the 999 images, and the lists are stored one after another with nothing in between, so the offsets are from the start of the file. StarEdit also reads the file. The layout is the same in every version from 1.04 to 1.17, of both StarCraft and Brood War. StarCraft 1.00 to 1.03 used an older layout with 755 images (28690 bytes); the older file is still in StarDat.mpq in later versions but is never loaded, because the copy in BrooDat.mpq (or patch_rt.mpq) is found first. The game loads the file once, when the program starts, together with scripts\iscript.bin and arr\images.tbl. Fields are read in order, and the game stops with a file error if the file is longer than the layout. A shorter file that ends exactly where a field ends loads without an error; the fields after the end then keep whatever they held before. No field is checked when the game uses it, so an out-of-range value reads whatever follows the table it points into.

Outside Brood War, the game and StarEdit only load the files of images 0 to 754; the higher images then have no graphics.

spec.name: GRP File
spec.description: A file number in arr\images.tbl, counting from 1; 0 means none. The game loads unit\<string> when the program starts, and stops with a fatal error if the file cannot be opened. An image with the same value as an earlier image in the same field shares its file. Nothing checks that an image has a GRP before drawing it.
spec.values: Integer value between 0 and the number of strings in arr\images.tbl.

spec.name: Graphic Turns
spec.description: Whether the image turns with its unit. If set, the GRP must have 17 frames for each animation frame: 17 directions over the right half of a turn, with the left half drawn mirrored. If clear, the frame is only what the animation script chooses. Only the lowest bit counts.

spec.name: Clickable
spec.description: Whether the image counts for clicking on its unit. The area that can be clicked is the box around the current frames of all clickable images of the sprite; if none is clickable, clicking the unit does not work reliably. Within that box, units with units.dat flag 0x100 can be clicked on a visible pixel of any clickable image, others only on a visible pixel of their main image. Only the lowest bit counts.

spec.name: Use Full Animation Script
spec.description: If clear, the image only plays the Init and Death entries of its animation script and ignores requests for the others (walking, attacking and so on). Only the lowest bit counts.

spec.name: Draw If Cloaked
spec.description: 0 hides the image while its unit is cloaked (shadows, engine glows). It also stops animation script commands that create a sprite (sprul, spruluselo) from creating one with this image while the unit is cloaked. Only images with Draw Function 0 get the cloaked look; visible images with another draw function keep drawing normally. StarEdit uses it when showing cloaked preplaced units.

spec.name: Draw Function
spec.description: How the image is drawn. Values 2 to 7, 12 and 16 are set by the game while it runs and are not used in the shipped file.
spec.values: Values above 17 are not checked and most likely crash the game when the image is drawn.

bits.value: Normal. The only value that cloaking and hallucination change
Normal, but stays normal on a cloaked or hallucinated unit (blood splats, Shield Battery charge, Installation doodads)
Cloaking (used by the game while a unit cloaks)
Cloaking, seen through (used by the game)
Cloaked, seen through (used by the game)
Decloaking, seen through (used by the game)
Colour remapping through the table chosen by Remapping (glows, fire, explosions)
Health bar: draws the hit point, shield and energy bar instead of the GRP
Protoss warp-in texture (used by the game)
Normal, in the colour of the player who owns the sprite (the Flag)
Draws only a green outline of the frame (building placement box)

spec.name: Remapping
spec.description: For Draw Function 9 only: which colour table the image is drawn through. Each table is loaded with the map from Tileset\<tileset>\<name>.pcx; every drawn pixel becomes table[GRP pixel, screen pixel]. Ignored for other draw functions.
spec.values: Values above 7 read past the list of tables. 0 with Draw Function 9 has no table and most likely crashes the game.

bits.value: bfire (blue fire, Protoss glows, shield hit)
trans50 (50% translucency, also used for cloaking)
red (one row only, so most GRP colours read past it)

spec.name: Animation Script
spec.description: The animation script (in scripts\iscript.bin) that runs the image. It is an ID that the game looks up in the script file's header, not a position; an ID that is not there stops the game with the fatal error "script %d does not exist". Several images can share a script.
spec.values: Integer value between 0 and 65535; must be an ID in iscript.bin.

spec.name: Shield Overlay
spec.description: A file number in arr\images.tbl, counting from 1; 0 means none. The game loads unit\<string> when the program starts, and stops with a fatal error if the file cannot be opened. An image with the same value as an earlier image in the same field shares its file. Where the shield flash (image 424) appears when the unit's shields are hit: the file has one list per direction the unit faces (17), with 32 points for the directions the hit comes from (not mirrored). The game uses it without checking for 0, but only for units with shields. Most unit images have protoss\mshield.los.
spec.values: Integer value between 0 and the number of strings in arr\images.tbl.

spec.name: Attack Overlay
spec.description: A file number in arr\images.tbl, counting from 1; 0 means none. The game loads unit\<string> when the program starts, and stops with a fatal error if the file cannot be opened. An image with the same value as an earlier image in the same field shares its file. The file is a list of points: for each frame of the image's GRP, a number of (x, y) offsets in pixels from the image, as signed bytes; x is mirrored with the image, and (127, 127) means no point. Used for the muzzle flashes of units firing from inside a Bunker (the bunker's own file, terran\pillbox.loa, one point for each of 8 directions) and by animation script commands that place graphics at an overlay point (imgoluselo and the like) with overlay 0. Not checked for 0.
spec.values: Integer value between 0 and the number of strings in arr\images.tbl.

spec.name: Damage Overlay
spec.description: A file number in arr\images.tbl, counting from 1; 0 means none. The game loads unit\<string> when the program starts, and stops with a fatal error if the file cannot be opened. An image with the same value as an earlier image in the same field shares its file. The file is a list of points: for each frame of the image's GRP, a number of (x, y) offsets in pixels from the image, as signed bytes; x is mirrored with the image, and (127, 127) means no point. Where the fires appear on a damaged building: none above 2/3 of its hit points, then more and larger fires as the hit points drop, at random points of the list. Up to 22 points of the first frame count. 0 means the unit never shows damage fires.
spec.values: Integer value between 0 and the number of strings in arr\images.tbl.

spec.name: Special Overlay
spec.description: A file number in arr\images.tbl, counting from 1; 0 means none. The game loads unit\<string> when the program starts, and stops with a fatal error if the file cannot be opened. An image with the same value as an earlier image in the same field shares its file. The file is a list of points: for each frame of the image's GRP, a number of (x, y) offsets in pixels from the image, as signed bytes; x is mirrored with the image, and (127, 127) means no point. Point 0 is where things attached to the image sit: the turret of a unit with a subunit (Siege Tank, Goliath), and overlays created by the animation script commands imgolorig and switchul. creategasoverlays n puts geyser smoke at point n. Also used by the *uselo script commands with overlay 2. Not checked for 0.
spec.values: Integer value between 0 and the number of strings in arr\images.tbl.

spec.name: Landing Dust Overlay
spec.description: A file number in arr\images.tbl, counting from 1; 0 means none. The game loads unit\<string> when the program starts, and stops with a fatal error if the file cannot be opened. An image with the same value as an earlier image in the same field shares its file. The file is a list of points: for each frame of the image's GRP, a number of (x, y) offsets in pixels from the image, as signed bytes; x is mirrored with the image, and (127, 127) means no point. Where dust appears when a building lands: dust sprites at points 0 to 8 and mirrored ones at points 16 to 24. 0 means no dust. Points 0 and 1 are also where the two units hatch from a Zergling or Scourge egg (zerg\zzebirth.lob, zerg\zavbirth.lob); that use is not checked for 0.
spec.values: Integer value between 0 and the number of strings in arr\images.tbl.

spec.name: Lift-off Dust Overlay
spec.description: A file number in arr\images.tbl, counting from 1; 0 means none. The game loads unit\<string> when the program starts, and stops with a fatal error if the file cannot be opened. An image with the same value as an earlier image in the same field shares its file. The file is a list of points: for each frame of the image's GRP, a number of (x, y) offsets in pixels from the image, as signed bytes; x is mirrored with the image, and (127, 127) means no point. Where dust appears when a building lifts off, used like Landing Dust Overlay. 0 means no dust. StarEdit shows it for buildings placed lifted.
spec.values: Integer value between 0 and the number of strings in arr\images.tbl.

appendices.name: Appendix: Images list
appendices.description: Every image, with its GRP file from arr\images.tbl in the shipped data (all under unit\). Images 755 to 998 only exist in Brood War.
